subagent_reports.architecture_assessment:
Design is coherent and within approved scope: it extends existing structural controls rather than adding parallel systems. Existing pattern: strict env-parse seam (config.rs from_vars + parse_*), SQL-structural safety (forget_manual source='manual' predicate, store.rs:251-260), runtime dim checks (embed.rs:53-60, scheduler.rs:161-175), bounded pool options (store.rs:24-31). Reference pattern: route new operator inputs through the tested config seam; prove static contracts with DB-free deterministic tests; rely on pgvector-documented defaults. Deviation: MINOR - the design leaves several HOW details unspecified (where to parse log level, how to derive the SQL dim, whether HNSW needs a forward migration, env-var name). Five leverage points collapse those to the simplest testable/default-equal forms.

=== SCOUT CANDIDATES (design mode, cap 5, sorted payoff/risk) ===

CANDIDATE A (design_around) | payoff medium | risk low | tie AC7/DDC3 | prior new
WHAT: Route the operator log-level parse through the existing Config::from_vars env-parse seam (mirroring parse_nonzero/parse_backend) and relocate the tracing_subscriber init from main.rs into run() (lib.rs:35-41, after Config::from_env() and before the first tracing::info!), passing cfg.log_level. Makes absent/invalid->INFO and valid->honored unit-testable like pool_size/backend, instead of an untestable parse buried in main.rs:12-15.
EVIDENCE: src/config.rs:56-125 + tests config.rs:202-366; src/main.rs:12-15 (no test seam); src/lib.rs:35-41 (config precedes first tracing call). NOTE: AC7 mandates lenient INFO fallback, which diverges from the strict present-but-invalid-errors policy of its siblings - document the intentional divergence.
RATIONALE: Reuses the proven tested pattern; mechanical relocation of a single subscriber; resolves the unspecified HOW with the simplest testable seam.

CANDIDATE B (design_around) | payoff medium | risk low | tie AC1/DDC1/SC1 | prior new
WHAT: Implement the dimension-contract proof as a DB-free unit test: include_str!("../migrations/0001_init.sql") + parse the embedding ... vector(N) literal and assert N == EMBEDDING_DIM. Avoids a heavier live-Postgres format_type introspection that would have to live in the #[ignore] integration suite.
EVIDENCE: migrations/0001_init.sql:37 (vector(1024)); src/types.rs:7 (EMBEDDING_DIM=1024); src/embed.rs:53-60 + src/scheduler.rs:161-175 (existing runtime dim checks); .github/workflows/ci.yml:33 (unit cargo test runs without Postgres). sqlx::migrate!("./migrations") (store.rs:47) already treats migrations as compile-time static inputs.
RATIONALE: Design specifies WHAT not HOW; include_str! is the simplest deterministic, infrastructure-free proof; narrow parse failure IS the drift signal.

CANDIDATE C (design_around) | payoff medium | risk low | tie AC6/DDC5 | prior new
WHAT: Because pgvector's HNSW defaults (m=16, ef_construction=64) EQUAL the values the design intends to state explicitly, adding WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64) to the EXISTING CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (migrations/0001_init.sql:50-51) is itself the migration-safe disposition: values are default-equal (zero behavior change) and IF NOT EXISTS leaves existing-database indexes untouched. No separate forward migration required.
EVIDENCE: pgvector README m=16/ef_construction=64 by default (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector); migrations/0001_init.sql:50-51 (no WITH clause today).
RATIONALE: Collapses the design's two-branch risk mitigation to the simpler no-op branch; the explicit-WITH edit is both documentation and safe no-op.

CANDIDATE D (design_around) | payoff medium | risk low | tie AC8 | prior new
WHAT: Since AC8 already changes Store::upsert's return to Result<()> and its sole caller ignores the value, have upsert delegate to upsert_batch(&[input.clone()], &[embedding.to_vec()]).map(|_| ()), deleting ~25 lines of duplicated INSERT/ON-CONFLICT SQL. One column list to evolve instead of two.
EVIDENCE: src/store.rs:52-78 (upsert) and :94-143 (upsert_batch) carry the identical 8-column INSERT + ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET clause verbatim; src/server.rs:115-121 (sole caller, ? ignores bool).
RATIONALE: DRY/campstone simplification adjacent to the scoped change. TRADEOFF: single-item remember path gains a begin/commit transaction (negligible for low-frequency interactive writes; single-statement rollback semantics unchanged) - validator to confirm.

CANDIDATE E (surface_to_user) | payoff medium | risk low | tie AC7 (naming convention) | prior new
WHAT: Resolve WHICH env var carries the operator log level: a namespaced EPISODE_LOG_LEVEL (matches the repo's exclusive EPISODE_* convention) vs the ecosystem-standard RUST_LOG (which .env.example:35 currently hints at and tracing_subscriber EnvFilter::from_default_env reads natively). The design names neither.
EVIDENCE: src/config.rs:60-72 (all vars EPISODE_*); .env.example:7-30 (every documented var EPISODE_*) and :35 (# RUST_LOG=episode=info commented hint); AC7 names no variable.
RATIONALE: Real ergonomics/convention tradeoff (repo consistency vs ecosystem familiarity) the contract leaves open; not auto-adoptable. EPISODE_LOG_LEVEL is more consistent; RUST_LOG is zero-extra-code via EnvFilter.

# Strengthen Episode Operations

## Objective

Make Episode operational contracts explicit, verifiable, and maintainable. Investigate all ten Tron findings, reconcile work already shipped, and remediate the net-new gaps.

## In Scope

1. Checked embedding-dimension compatibility across Rust, model output, and SQL schema.
2. Materialized project/spec context and README configuration accuracy.
3. Release-profile CI compilation.
4. Evidence-led DB-pool contention and ingestion-cadence decisions.
5. Explicit HNSW defaults with migration-safe handling.
6. Operator log-level control while preserving stderr-only MCP hygiene.
7. Correct `upsert` API semantics.
8. Evidence-led multilingual embedding disposition.
9. Regression protection for manual-memory deletion boundaries.

## Finding Disposition Map

| Finding | Discovery disposition | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 dimension drift | Open: add checked schema/Rust compatibility proof | `src/types.rs:7`; `migrations/0001_init.sql:37`; `src/embed.rs:53-60` |
| 2 missing context/specs | Open: materialize durable context; also resolve README `.env.example` drift | `project.json:3,6,8`; `README.md:64` |
| 3 release CI | Open: add release build verification | `.github/workflows/ci.yml:28-33`; `Cargo.toml:27-31` |
| 4 pool contention | Partially shipped: acquisition bounds exist; measurement decision remains | `src/store.rs:24-31`; `tests/pool_bounds.rs` |
| 5 HNSW | Open: make documented defaults explicit, not speculative tuning | `migrations/0001_init.sql:51` |
| 6 logging | Open: env-configurable level with INFO fallback and stderr writer | `src/main.rs:12-15`; `src/lib.rs:37` |
| 7 serial ingestion | Partially shipped: batches bounded; cadence/parallelism measurement remains | `src/lib.rs:280-298` |
| 8 upsert boolean | Open: remove unused boolean rather than invent insert/update semantics | `src/store.rs:52-78`; `src/server.rs:115-121` |
| 9 multilingual embeddings | Open: decide from product need and model/schema evidence | `src/embed.rs:35` |
| 10 deletion predicate | Already shipped: retain and prove SQL-enforced source/namespace restriction | `src/store.rs:251-260`; `tests/recall_it.rs` |

## Discovery Findings

### Current State

Episode is a Rust stdio MCP server. `EpisodeServer` routes recall, remember, forget, and stats through a bounded priority scheduler to a single embedding worker and PostgreSQL/pgvector persistence (`src/lib.rs:35-94`; `src/server.rs`; `src/scheduler.rs:252-263`). The prior archived resilience change already established bounded pool acquisition, bounded batch processing, and deletion restriction tests.

### Edge Cases

- Dimension: model output mismatch; existing databases with the older vector dimension.
- CI: release-only LTO/link errors; debug build passing while release build fails.
- Pool/ingestion: unavailable DB versus saturated pool; a cycle lasting longer than its configured interval.
- HNSW: fresh databases versus already-created index; unmeasured tuning worsening recall/build time.
- Logging: invalid level input; stdout corruption in stdio transport.
- Upsert: update versus insert semantics; future caller branching on a non-meaningful boolean.
- Documentation: missing declared path; README setup command naming a nonexistent template.
- Multilingual support: English-only workload; mixed-language workload without a justified model migration.
- Deletion: wrong namespace; ingested source; repeated deletion.

### Related Pattern Scan

Related safety patterns already exist: strict environment parsing (`src/config.rs:89-171`), output-dimension validation (`src/embed.rs:53-60`; `src/scheduler.rs:161`), SQL-enforced manual deletion (`src/store.rs:251-260`), and bounds tests (`tests/pool_bounds.rs:21-70`). The change will extend those mechanisms rather than create parallel policy.

### LBP Check

Likely direction follows the established stack: use checked invariants and tests for schema/model compatibility; use Cargo release compilation for release proof; use `tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter` with explicit INFO fallback while retaining stderr; preserve pgvector HNSW defaults explicitly rather than tune without measurements. External evidence: pgvector documents HNSW defaults `m=16`, `ef_construction=64` (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector); tracing-subscriber documents that `EnvFilter::from_default_env()` otherwise falls back to ERROR (https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/latest/src/tracing_subscriber/filter/env/mod.rs.html). No service or platform replacement is warranted.

### Draft Spec Deltas

- `rq-episode-dimension-contract01`: Given model output and schema configuration, when an embedding batch is accepted, then the accepted dimension matches the authoritative contract before persistence.
- `rq-episode-release-build01`: Given a supported pull request, when CI runs, then release-profile compilation completes successfully.
- `rq-episode-operator-logging01`: Given a valid operator log-level setting, when Episode starts, then logs use that level, retain INFO as the default, and remain on stderr.
- `rq-episode-manual-forget01`: Given a memory outside the requested namespace or from a non-manual source, when deletion is requested, then no record is deleted.

### Completeness Verification

Problem completeness: high confidence. The ten reported findings were reconciled against implementation and the resilience archive; two are already substantially addressed and one is fully shipped. Scope completeness: medium confidence. Primary operation surfaces are scheduler, store, embed, server, config, CI, schema, and repository documentation. No claim of a sole global chokepoint is required. Secondary surfaces: archive-only contract material is in scope for context recovery; PostgreSQL/model replacement is explicitly out of scope; model replacement stays unresolved pending product decision.

### Ambiguity Analysis

- `F1 MEDIUM Functional Scope`: proposal says “all ten” while discovery shows findings 4, 7, and 10 were partially or fully shipped. Evidence: “investigating and addressing all ten Tron reconnaissance findings.” Resolution: the disposition map preserves all ten and scopes only net-new remediation.
- `S1 MEDIUM Completion Signals`: pool, cadence, and multilingual items need measurable or user-confirmed outcomes before implementation. Evidence: “Measure and remediate database-pool contention risk” and “Investigate multilingual embedding support.” Resolution: agreement will require bounded measurement evidence and a product decision.
- `M1 LOW Missing Information`: production language needs are not documented. Evidence: “Investigate multilingual embedding support against actual product needs.” Resolution: user decision required.

Coverage: B:C F:P S:P M:P

## Constraints

- Preserve stored-vector compatibility unless an explicit migration is designed and tested.
- Protect interactive recall latency from background ingestion.
- Use evidence and tests rather than heuristic capacity conclusions.
- Keep schema changes migration-safe.
- Do not replace PostgreSQL/pgvector, MCP transport, or embedding model without evidence and explicit scope approval.

## Out of Scope

- Unmeasured capacity redesign.
- Broad unrelated refactors.
- Model replacement without a confirmed product requirement and compatibility plan.

## Discovery Opportunity Scout

Triggered: broad architecture and operational scope. Five candidates considered; five low-risk, contract-tied recommendations adopted into the draft direction: archive reconciliation, `Result<()>` upsert semantics, release CI compilation, explicit documented HNSW defaults, and INFO-preserving EnvFilter behavior. Measurement decisions remain open for pool, cadence, and multilingual support.

# Problem Statement

The Episode MCP server has ten reconnaissance findings spanning correctness, operational readiness, performance risk, observability, and documentation. The product needs a bounded investigation and remediation change rather than isolated fixes, because the findings cross the ingestion, embedding, persistence, CI, and ADV-contract surfaces.

## Evidence

- Embedding dimension is duplicated across Rust, the SQL schema, and model assumptions (`src/types.rs:7`, `migrations/0001_init.sql:37`, `src/embed.rs:35`).
- Declared project/spec locations are missing, leaving durable contract material in code comments and an archive (`project.json:3,6,8`; `src/lib.rs:144-155`; `src/scheduler.rs:1`; `src/store.rs:90`).
- CI does not build the release profile (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:28-33`; `Cargo.toml:27-31`; `scripts/deploy.sh:9`).
- Ingestion and interactive operations share a DB pool without saturation coverage (`src/store.rs:94-143`; `src/config.rs:63`).
- HNSW tuning is implicit (`migrations/0001_init.sql:51`), log level is fixed (`src/main.rs:12-15`), root ingestion is serial (`src/lib.rs:280-298`), and the upsert boolean is semantically misleading (`src/store.rs:52-78`).
- Additional investigation is needed for multilingual embedding quality and SQL predicate regression protection (`src/embed.rs:35`; `src/store.rs:251-260`).

## Root Cause Analysis

The findings share a root cause: key runtime and operational contracts are distributed across source, schema, deployment, and archived documentation without a single enforced authority or complete production-oriented verification path. This allows configuration/schema drift, leaves capacity behavior unmeasured, and makes recovery/maintenance knowledge difficult to discover.

Contributing factors:

1. Model/schema compatibility is expressed by repeated literals rather than a checked contract.
2. Operational validation stops at debug-profile CI and excludes release/profile-specific proof.
3. Persistence and ingestion performance choices lack bounded load evidence and explicit tuning rationale.
4. The intended ADV/spec structure was declared but not materialized.

## Desired Outcome

Investigate every finding, implement safe in-scope remediation where evidence supports it, and document any item that must remain deferred with a measured rationale and explicit follow-up boundary.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Keep the existing Rust MCP server architecture. Changes are localized to repository metadata/docs, CI workflows, release workflow, configuration/log initialization, persistence/schema compatibility checks, and focused tests. Interactive request scheduling remains unchanged; capacity work is measurement-first.

## Key Decisions

1. **Dimension contract:** retain `EMBEDDING_DIM` as Rust authority; a DB-free `include_str!` test parses the migration dimension and compares it to the constant. Runtime output validation remains the rejection point before persistence (`src/embed.rs:53-60`; `src/scheduler.rs:161`); `Store::upsert_batch` is the persistence lever (`src/store.rs:94-143`).
2. **Documentation:** create repository operations/setup documentation and declared ADV context; correct README paths.
3. **CI and releases:** add a release-profile build to current CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:28-33`). Add a main-only `workflow_run` release workflow that requires successful CI, uses scoped permissions and concurrency, publishes a versioned release, changelog, and documented artifacts, and never publishes from PRs.
4. **HNSW:** use `WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64)` on the existing idempotent index statement. These equal pgvector documented defaults, so this is explicit documentation rather than tuning (`migrations/0001_init.sql:51`).
5. **Logging:** add `EPISODE_LOG_LEVEL` through the tested config seam (`src/config.rs:56-125`), move tracing initialization behind an injectable/testable boundary, default invalid or absent input to INFO, and retain stderr-only output.
6. **Upsert API:** change `Store::upsert` to `Result<()>` and delegate duplicate SQL behavior to `upsert_batch`; transaction overhead for a single remember is acknowledged and bounded.
7. **Measurement-led operations:** add bounded reproducible evidence before scheduler/pool changes. Ingestion lever: `src/lib.rs:280-298`; pool construction lever: `src/store.rs:24-31`.
8. **Deletion and language boundaries:** retain SQL source/namespace predicate and integration coverage; document English-only support with no model change.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Reconcile archive coverage; write project/spec/setup documentation.
2. Add deterministic migration/constant and API tests; retain deletion tests.
3. Add testable `EPISODE_LOG_LEVEL` configuration, INFO fallback, and stderr logging.
4. Add release-profile CI build and CI-gated automated release workflow.
5. Make HNSW defaults explicit in the idempotent index definition.
6. Add bounded pool/ingestion measurements; record a no-change or change disposition.
7. Verify test suite, release build, CI workflow, and release workflow validation.

## LBP Analysis

Extends existing structural controls rather than adding a second scheduler, datastore, model, or release platform. It retains pgvector defaults, proves the release build before publishing, and treats capacity changes as evidence-dependent.

## Affected Components

`src/{config,types,embed,scheduler,store,server,main,lib}.rs`; `migrations/0001_init.sql`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` plus release workflow; `README.md`, `.env.example`, `project.md`, `.adv/specs/`, `docs/`; focused unit/integration tests.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: Dimension mismatch proof fails deterministically without a live database.
- DDC2: Release publishing has no PR path and requires successful CI.
- DDC3: Application logs never use stdout.
- DDC4: Capacity evidence states workload, duration, pool configuration, and measured outcome.
- DDC5: HNSW/documentation changes preserve existing databases.

## Risks / Mitigations

- Missing release permissions: preserve CI proof, surface publishing configuration as external blocker; never bypass it.
- Static migration parse brittleness: a parse failure is a deliberate schema-contract drift signal.
- Measurement environment differs from production: label evidence bounded; do not extrapolate capacity.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Auto-adopted four contract-tied low-risk improvements: config-seam logging, DB-free migration/constant proof, documented-default HNSW clause, and `upsert_batch` delegation. Agent-resolved environment variable name: `EPISODE_LOG_LEVEL`, consistent with existing configuration namespace. No user-value tradeoff.

## Independent Validation

Validator: clean pass. All SC1–SC3, AC1–AC12, C1–C4, DONT1–DONT4, and OOS1–OOS2 trace to this design. Verified source levers include dimension/schema locations, upsert caller and batch transaction, config seam, stderr logging, deletion SQL, debug-only CI, release profile, and serial ingestion. No contract compromise or blocker. Planning must preserve the acknowledged single-item transaction overhead and implement a structurally CI-gated, main-only release trigger with concurrency and least-privilege permissions.
